comparator.name: Criminology (Criminologie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted OER prescribes ten 6-EC courses in each of Years 1 and 2. Year 3 has four compulsory components (6, 6, 12, 6 EC) and 30 EC of genuinely open minor/elective space. The 12-EC research-skills unit includes group investigation and an individual thesis; it is not split into invented extra credits. Zero-credit professional identity line and embedded language test are excluded. The Forensic Criminology minor is an optional example, not a compulsory specialization.
components: Aard, omvang en schade van criminaliteit

Research skills project with group investigation and individual thesis.
Genuinely open 30-EC first-semester minor or approved coherent elective period, including possible exchange; Forensische Criminologie is one option, not a requirement.

core: Crime, criminal law and responses by justice institutions
Psychological and life-course explanations of offending and victimisation
Social causes, harms and prevention of crime
Quantitative and qualitative empirical criminological research
adjacent: Media narratives about crime and the social meaning of justice
Violent conflict, social trust and public safety
questions: Why do individuals offend, and how do life-course and mental-health factors matter?
How do legal and social institutions prevent and punish crime?
What evidence can clarify crime, its harms and responses?

alternatives.label: Crime, behavior and justice
alternatives.concept: Combines criminal law and institutions with social and psychological explanations of offending, empirical methods, public responses and representations of crime. UCR offers a substantial related interdisciplinary path but does not teach VU’s dedicated criminology sequence, policing practice, victimology or supervised criminology thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Law, psychology, sociology and methods jointly organize the complete curriculum around offending and society’s response.
progression: Six four-course semesters in Fall 2026–Spring 2029; PPD in Year 1, at least six 300-level courses, official offerings and all earlier formal prerequisites checked against the enriched workbook. Introductory law, sociology, brain/behavior and methods generally precede advanced courses.

selection.assessment: The closest response combines law, psychology, sociology and methods. Cybercrime and forensic criminology are evidenced possible directions, but UCR lacks a specialist digital-offending/security sequence and forensic crime-scene or forensic-methods sequence. A second 24-course programme would rely on general adjacent material rather than a distinct defensible criminology route.

notes.text: VU teaches a dedicated criminology sequence in crime measurement, theoretical and historical criminology, substantive and procedural criminal law, victimology, prevention and a 12-EC criminological research project, alongside 30 EC of open elective space. UCR can combine relevant law, psychology, sociology and methods but does not reproduce that specialized sequence or the individual thesis.
